Could the Commanders handle this late-game scenario? The game management wasn’t the issue here, but the result wasn’t any better. The game was in the balance, with the Commanders pushing hard for a score with less that an minute left. In the decisive play, Daniels was called for an intentional grounding call that generated a loss of down and a 10 second runoff, setting up a presumptive last-second chuck into the end zone. Jayden Daniels’ final pass never left his hand, leaving this comeback attempt just short of a miracle finish. Jayden Daniels gets sacked as time expires. 49ers win 23-17 pic.twitter.com/7NMR0apwfI — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) October 20, 2026 The Commanders lost this one 23-17, a heartbreaker that drops the Commanders to 1-4-1 on the season heading into their bye. Here are some key takeaways from this Week 6 defeat: Dan Quinn’s seat cools a bit The Commanders attempted to convert a fourth down in the first half that went completely wrong. They were flagged for an illegal shift on the play, but quarterback Jayden Daniels threw the ball away over working to complete a pass that would earn a first down. It was a messy play that has become all too common. Then a video clip from the broadcast went viral, where Quinn seemed to look confused about what down it was. This is a very tough look for Dan Quinn. Looks like he thought the 4th down play was 3rd down. Very tough especially after last week pic.twitter.com/KUU8D2S81d — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) October 20, 2026 Whether that was the case or not, it was a bad look after letting the clock run out in overtime against the Giants and within makeable range of a decisive field goal. Back to what we discussed in the intro, Quinn needed a solid performance and signs of hope for better following what happened in Week 5. Netflix/The Ringer reporter Tom Pelissero stated that owner Josh Harris preferred to not make an in-season change but would be following Monday night’s game closely and barring signs the team had given up or blowout losses, he preferred to let Quinn try and turn things around. With that in mind, will Harris admire the Commanders fight in the second half? They were within one possession late against a super-talented 49ers team and it was clear late in this game that the Commanders showed fight. The Commanders cut a once massive deficit to one possession with a Jayden Daniels pass to Rachaad White, one of many plays by the star quarterback that got Washington back in the game. . @Chaad_1 in the endzone ‼️ 📺 #WASvsSF on ESPN pic.twitter.com/2wABqdIg3B — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 20, 2026 The Commanders were driving for a go-ahead score inside of two minutes, but a fourth-and-3 was not converted and put the Commanders in a bind. Bottom line: The Commanders showed fight. That’s a data point Harris will consider as he evaluates what comes next. Daronte Jones flips the script The Commanders entered Week 6 allowing red-zone touchdowns on 83.33% of the time. Yeah. You read that right. That’s obviously worst in the league, and the Commanders didn’t do a lot better. The 49ers kept on scoring from inside Washington’s 20-yard line, facing little resistance on the way past the goal line. The Commanders had been getting beat often when their heavy blitz rate didn’t produce pressure early on, and Jones brought the heat far less often against the 49ers and a quarterback in Brock Purdy who knows how to exploit it. The first half stats were wild, with San Francisco averaging 7.4 yards per play. The Commanders looked wiped and at a complete loss for how to attack the 49ers. After allowing 20 points in the first half, the Commanders gave up just three in the second half. What a freaking turn. Jones started to blitz a lot more in the second half and to great effect, including this Odafe Oweh sack, generated by an interior blitz, that gave the Commanders a chance. Defense forces a three-and-out 🙌 📺 #WASvsSF on ESPN pic.twitter.com/8Pu2T3vA5g — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 20, 2026 The Commanders got consecutive three-and-outs in the fourth quarter to allow for a real comeback attempt, which was alive with 52 seconds to go. It fell short, but the Commanders defense got better as the game went on. There’s still plenty to work on, but the second half was an encouraging sign after the disaster that was the first half. Losing Terry McLaurin a nightmare scenario Commanders star receiver Terry McLaurin suffered a knee injury in the first quarter that, well, did not look good. Per the broadcast feed, McLaurin’s knee seemed to buckle as if structurally unsound. Terry goes down and immediately grabs his left knee pic.twitter.com/7EtIvcTsmM — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 20, 2026 He tried to get off the field but eventually went to the ground. He was treated there by trainers, with teammates all around him. An air cast was placed on his leg and he was carted off the field. Terry McLaurin wearing a large air cast on his left leg as he hobbles onto the cart. pic.twitter.com/am35L8NF3b — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) October 20, 2026 We won’t know the exact nature of the injury until later Monday or Tuesday, but there should be a high level of concern that he’ll miss extended time. That would be a nightmare scenario for a team left reeling after a rough start to the season. McLaurin is a locker-room leader and the team’s most talented catcher, someone who draws defensive attention and makes life easier on others. While the Commanders have a deep receiver room, his loss would be immeasurable for a team that needs as many talented players as possible. We don’t want to speculate about the length of his absence or even the exact injury diagnosis, but it’s fair to say his loss had a negative impact on this game – he had Washington’s only explosive play of the first half – and was a somber note on a rough night in the Bay Area.

item.title: Grizzlies shock NBA fans with stunning decision to cut former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr.
item.description: Grizzlies shock NBA fans with stunning decision to cut former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr. originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Memphis Grizzlies made a surprising roster decision Monday, waiving former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr. and guard Micah Peavy ahead of the NBA's deadline to finalize regular-season rosters. According to ESPN's Shams Charania, Memphis released both players to meet the league's 15-player roster limit before the start of the 2026-27 season. The decision involving Clayton is particularly surprising considering his draft status and potential as a young guard. Clayton, selected 18th overall by the Utah Jazz in the 2025 NBA Draft, joined Memphis in February as part of the blockbuster trade that sent former Defensive Player of the Year Jaren Jackson Jr. to Utah. During his 24 appearances with the Grizzlies last season, Clayton averaged 9.7 points, 5.7 assists and 2.1 rebounds per game. Grizzlies make bold roster shakeup Despite showing flashes of promise, Clayton struggled to establish himself as a consistent contributor. Memphis reportedly explored potential trades before ultimately deciding to release the second-year guard. According to NBA insider Marc Stein, the Sacramento Kings emerged as a possible destination during trade discussions, but no agreement materialized. Clayton previously enjoyed a successful college career at Florida, helping lead the Gators to the 2025 NCAA national championship while earning Final Four Most Outstanding Player honors. Meanwhile, Peavy was selected 40th overall in the 2025 draft and spent his rookie season with the New Orleans Pelicans . He appeared in 61 games, averaging 4.3 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.0 assists before joining Memphis through a September trade. An ankle injury limited Peavy's opportunity to compete for a roster spot during training camp. For Memphis, the moves reflect a commitment to reshaping its roster around younger talent while creating opportunities for players already established within the organization. However, releasing Clayton could eventually become a decision the Grizzlies regret if the former Florida standout develops into a productive NBA guard elsewhere. Both players will now have opportunities to continue their professional careers with another franchise as Memphis prepares for Wednesday's season opener against Utah. item.title: Colts’ Shane Steichen isn’t ready to bail on Daniel Jones for Anthony Richardson just yet
item.description: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) runs off the field Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, following the game against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Colts’ Shane Steichen isn’t ready to bail on Daniel Jones for Anthony Richardson just yet appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Shane Steichen ’s Indianapolis Colts are 2-4 on the season heading into Week 7, a rough start that led to the firing of GM Chris Ballard . An injury update to Alec Pierce also dropped as the Colts’ passing game, and starting QB situation, came into focus. Colts writer James Boyd of The Athletic shared a new update on the Daniel Jones vs. Anthony Richardson race, which included Steichen’s choice heading into a game against the Vikings in Minneapolis. “Colts HC Shane Steichen says QB Daniel Jones will remain the team’s starter against the Vikings,” Boyd wrote. “DC Lou Anarumo will continue to call the defense as well.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jones has worked to become a better passer but hasn’t been the most proficient QB by a long shot in 2026. He has over 1,200 yards passing but has also thrown six interceptions against four touchdown passes. His rushing yards average has dropped in each of the last five seasons, from 5.0 yards per carry in 2022 to 3.2 in 2026. Anthony Richardson, the Colts’ former first round pick, has yet to play this season, a surprising development considering his immense football gifts. Jones admitted he is hurting his team with turnovers and must do a better job in Week 7 against the Vikings, one of the NFL’s toughest defenses. Now in his eighth NFL season, Jones is starting to skate on thin ice as a quarterback whose best skills aren’t quite what they used to be and a player who hasn’t been able to shore up his glaring deficiencies as a thrower and caretaker of the football. The Colts need a win as badly as any team in the NFL, and Week 7 looks like a low probability-win game against Kyler Murray and the Vikings. If Jones doesn’t pull a rabbit out of his hat on the road against one of the league’s best defenses, Steichen may have no choice but to turn to Richardson by the time Week 8 rolls around. Related: Expected Colts’ Alec Pierce injury update puts extra damper on already-terrible week Related: What Colts’ Shane Steichen said about Chris Ballard firing after Titans loss

item.title: Former Colts GM Chris Ballard Foreshadowed His Own Demise
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 25: General manager Chris Ballard of the Indianapolis Colts speaks to the media during the NFL Scouting Combine at the Indiana Convention Center on February 25, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty The news many disgruntled Indianapolis Colts fans were waiting to hear for years was announced Monday. The team is moving on longtime GM Chris Ballard following Sunday’s ugly loss to the Tennessee Titans. That drops the Colts to 2-4 on the season and at risk of missing the postseason for the sixth consecutive year. Ownership decided it was finally time. A clip from July shows how even Ballard himself knew his seat was hot at the start of the season. Chris Ballard Wanted to Prove Himself Ballard got very honest back in July when asked if he deserved a contract extension. His response? “No, I wouldn’t do one,” he said. “I’m in the last year of my deal, we need to win.” 2026 marked his 10th year as general manager of the Colts, which is almost an unheard of tenure for an NFL GM. The most curious part of it all was how he retained his job with suboptimal results. #Colts general manager Chris Ballard is on the last year of his contract. Does he expect a contract extension before the season? "No. I wouldn't do one… We need to win." pic.twitter.com/3IrqSWDr2F — WISH-TV News (@WISHNews8) July 28, 2026 The Colts last made the postseason during the 2020 season, falling to the Buffalo Bills in the first round. The team hasn’t won a playoff game since the 2018 season, and the duo of Ballard and Shane Steichen just posted back-to-back 8-9 finishes. Ballard was both self-aware and honest when discussing his own contract. His prediction ended up coming true and the team is left in a weird position for the remainder of the season. Colts Still Have Big Decisions to Make The Colts are not out of postseason contention, even at 2-4 and after losing to the previously 0-5 Titans. But the new front office, and ownership, will have to decide if they will try to compete or if they want to trade away top talent in order to restock draft capital for the future. The NFL trade deadline arrives on November 10, giving this Colts team three more games to prove the roster shouldn’t be dismantled. Yet even if the Colts are 5-4 at that point, it may not be enough to pass up on some intriguing trade offers. Quenton Nelson is a free agent after the season, and so is DeForest Buckner. Trading both could bring back some solid draft capital for a team that saw Ballard send two first-round picks to the New York Jets last season for Sauce Gardner. That was just one of many gambles that set the team back before he was fired. The two biggest remaining decisions have to do with Steichen and quarterback Daniel Jones. A playoff victory may be the only thing that can save the coach’s job, and even that may not be enough if the next GM wants their own pick at head coach. "No. I wouldn't do one… We need to win." pic.twitter.com/3IrqSWDr2F — WISH-TV News (@WISHNews8) July 28, 2026 The Colts last made the postseason during the 2020 season, falling to the Buffalo Bills in the first round. The Colts may as well see what he can do if a rebuild is on the horizon in 2027. Plenty of Colts fans got what they wanted with this Ballard dismissal. However, waiting until now to do it may have set the organization back even further than it was six weeks ago. item.title: Vikings Insider Thinks Team Could Trade For Franchise Legend’s Son
item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Head coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings looks on during the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Vikings are one of three remaining undefeated teams, and they might be one of only two if the Commanders can pull off an upset over the 49ers on Monday night. Meanwhile, the Buccaneers haven’t enjoyed nearly as much success over the first six weeks of the season. They’re currently last place in the NFC South with a 1-5 record. That fact has led The Athletic ‘s Alec Lewis to theorize whether they might be sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline. If they do prove to be a sinking ship (no pun intended), he believes Kevin O’Connell and Co. could swing a deal to acquire a player who might ring a bell for Vikings faithful, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. “Taking a swing will be worth a conversation if players such as Antoine Winfield Jr. or Budda Baker are available,” Lewis wrote. “The Vikings would also be smart to think about a contingency plan for Smith in the form of an elite player with blitzing savvy and presnap deciphering chops.” Antoine Winfield Jr. Has Followed In His Father’s Footsteps The apple didn’t fall far from the tree when it comes to Antoine Winfield Jr. His father, appropriately named Antoine Winfield Sr., was selected by the Buffalo Bills in the first round of the 1999 NFL Draft. While his career might have begun in Eastern New York, he ascended to stardom after signing with the Vikings ahead of the 2004 NFL season. He made three Pro Bowl appearances over his nine years in Minnesota and was one of the league’s toughest cornerbacks of his generation. What he made up for in size (5’9″, 180 lbs.), he more than made up for in heart. He regularly finished near the league lead in tackles among cover men and was always around the ball. Winfield Sr. was also honored by being named one of the 50 Greatest Vikings on the team’s 50th anniversary in 2010. Meanwhile, Winfield Jr. is the same height, but packs an even bigger punch thanks to his 203-pound frame. The 28-year-old has been one of the Buccaneers’ best players since the team selected him in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft, and has two Pro Bowls under his belt. Winfield Jr. has been a unique chess piece for the Bucs defense, with 18 career sacks and 9 interceptions to show for it. He’s also shown the same tenacity against the run as his father, eclipsing 80 tackles every season where he’s played at least 13 games. Either player would be an incredible chess piece for defensive coordinator Brian Flores to deploy, and they’d ensure the post-Harrison Smith safety landscape is secure. They’d also be potentially low-cost options (or at least lower than players of their caliber should be), with both the Bucs and Cardinals already having one eye on 2028. item.title: 49ers escape Week 6 with a win over the Commanders after a second-half letdown
item.description: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jordan James took the opening kickoff to the 36-yard line for the San Francisco 49ers. Jordan Watkins started at wide receiver opposite Mike Evans. Jacob Cowing came in on the first third down. Evans caught a 25-yard pass on the first play. Kaelon Black converted on 3rd-and-1. The offense quickly got into the red zone. Brock Purdy’s first target to George Kittle went for a touchdown, giving the 49ers a 7-0 lead. It was the third time the Niners began the game with a touchdown drive this season. Purdy went 5-for-6 on a 9-play, four-minute drive. Jayden Daniels found Terry McLaurin on what looked like a busted coverage to begin Washington’s first drive for 27 yards. But their drive stalled after Luke Gifford limited Daniels’ scramble to three yards, and Malik Mustapha spooked Stefon Diggs into a drop. That meant the Commanders would settle for a 51-yard field goal to make it 7-3. So much for any Achilles injury or soreness, Evans gained 54 yards to start the Niners’ second drive. Once again, they were in the red zone. But Christian McCaffrey lost three yards on a screen pass, and Connor Colby’s false start gave the Niners 3rd and long. The offense stayed on the field for 4th and 3. Purdy looked right, didn’t see anything that he liked, so scrambled for the first down. On third-and-goal from the one-yard line, Christian McCaffrey punched it in to give the Niners their second consecutive scoring drive. This drive took a little under five minutes on 8 plays. Eddy Pineiro missed another extra point, making it 13-3. It is the kind of miss you can’t turn a blind eye to, as they add up. Luke Farrell was flagged for a facemask on the kickoff, gifting Washington great field position. A Daniels scramble was negated after Romello Height drew a holding flag. Daniels fled the pocket because Gracen Halton won. On third and 9, Osa Odighizuwa sacked Daniels, forcing the punt. Raheem Morris’s blitz gave everybody a 1-on-1, and Odighizuwa rewarded him with a sack. On the same play, the cart came out for McLaurin, which is the last thing you want to see. Jacob Cowing inexplicably fielded a punt, then muffed it, giving the Commanders a 58-yard gain in field position. Evans was held on one play. He couldn’t hold on to a third-down target, and the 49ers punted on their third drive. Washington had another bust on its third drive. Two players were guarding one, leaving Chig Okonkwo open 35 yards downfield. He stepped out of bounds six yards earlier, for a 29-yard gain. Nonetheless, Washington was knocking on the door once more. Daniels was stopped short of the sticks on third down, forcing a 4th-and-2. But Daniels threw it away, and the Niners forced a red-zone stop. Purdy found Jordan Watkins for a gain of 22. Then Brandin Cooks for 13 on a now slant. As the 49ers were driving, McCaffrey fumbled for the first time this season and gave the ball right back to Washington. But Gracen Halton drew a holding call and sacked D

Jordan Watkins started at wide receiver opposite Mike Evans. Jacob Cowing came in on the first third down. Evans caught a 25-yard pass on the first play. Kaelon Black converted on 3rd-and-1. The offense quickly got into the red zone. Brock Purdy’s first target to George Kittle went for a touchdown, giving the 49ers a 7-0 lead. It was the third time the Niners began the game with a touchdown drive this season. Purdy went 5-for-6 on a 9-play, four-minute drive. Jayden Daniels found Terry McLaurin on what looked like a busted coverage to begin Washington’s first drive for 27 yards. But their drive stalled after Luke Gifford limited Daniels’ scramble to three yards, and Malik Mustapha spooked Stefon Diggs into a drop. That meant the Commanders would settle for a 51-yard field goal to make it 7-3. So much for any Achilles injury or soreness, Evans gained 54 yards to start the Niners’ second drive. Once again, they were in the red zone. But Christian McCaffrey lost three yards on a screen pass, and Connor Colby’s false start gave the Niners 3rd and long. The offense stayed on the field for 4th and 3. Purdy looked right, didn’t see anything that he liked, so scrambled for the first down. On third-and-goal from the one-yard line, Christian McCaffrey punched it in to give the Niners their second consecutive scoring drive. This drive took a little under five minutes on 8 plays. Eddy Pineiro missed another extra point, making it 13-3. It is the kind of miss you can’t turn a blind eye to, as they add up. Luke Farrell was flagged for a facemask on the kickoff, gifting Washington great field position. A Daniels scramble was negated after Romello Height drew a holding flag. Daniels fled the pocket because Gracen Halton won. On third and 9, Osa Odighizuwa sacked Daniels, forcing the punt. Raheem Morris’s blitz gave everybody a 1-on-1, and Odighizuwa rewarded him with a sack. On the same play, the cart came out for McLaurin, which is the last thing you want to see. Jacob Cowing inexplicably fielded a punt, then muffed it, giving the Commanders a 58-yard gain in field position. Evans was held on one play. He couldn’t hold on to a third-down target, and the 49ers punted on their third drive. Washington had another bust on its third drive. Two players were guarding one, leaving Chig Okonkwo open 35 yards downfield. He stepped out of bounds six yards earlier, for a 29-yard gain. Nonetheless, Washington was knocking on the door once more. Daniels was stopped short of the sticks on third down, forcing a 4th-and-2. But Daniels threw it away, and the Niners forced a red-zone stop. Purdy found Jordan Watkins for a gain of 22. Then Brandin Cooks for 13 on a now slant. As the 49ers were driving, McCaffrey fumbled for the first time this season and gave the ball right back to Washington. But Gracen Halton drew a holding call and sacked Daniels, so all was forgiven. That holding penalty was the most by a 49ers defensive tackle since DeForest Buckner was on the roster. It’s another way to quantify impact. Farrell had another penalty; this one was costly. Instead of 1st and goal from the seven, it was third and long. But Purdy scrambled his way out of trouble once more. He picked up a first down on 3rd and 11. He ran right by Sonny Styles. Trent Williams was flagged for holding right after, putting the offense back behind the sticks. After Evans picked up a first down, he limped off the field and into the locker room. During the timeout, Evans looked like he was stretching his Achilles. He left the game with 94 yards. Purdy kept the ball on fourth down to pick up a first down. McCaffrey finished it off, giving the 49ers a commanding 20-3 lead. It was a 14-play drive that took over six minutes off the clock without giving Washington another possession. The 49ers had 17 first downs compared to the 16 total plays run by Washington. Washington received the ball to begin the third quarter. They got their third first down of the game after Treylon Burks caught an 18-yard pass. Romello Height drew a holding call. Keion White forced a false start. The defense got the Commanders into another third-and-long situation. On 3rd and 8, Daniels ran into Mykel Williams, his first sack of the season. The Commanders were 0-for on third down after they picked up their third sack of the evening. The offensive line picked up Washington’s 6-man pressure, allowing Purdy to find Kittle for a gain of 35. A third-down pass was tipped, and the offense had a rare trip into the red zone that didn’t result in a touchdown. Pineiro’s 33-yard try was good, making it 23-3. Washington answered with an 11-play drive that took over five minutes. Jayden Daniels kept the drive alive on a 4th-and-five to Diggs before finding him in the end zone. That made it 23-10. Brock Purdy ran into trouble to end the third quarter, and the Niners offense would face another second-and-forever. Purdy navigated the pocket well on third down, but Kittle had the pass poked away, leaving it to Corliss Waitman’s second punt. It looked like another McCaffrey fumble, but Christian’s brother didn’t touch the ball on replay, and the Commanders retained possession. The 49ers were fortunate to avoid a helmet-to-helmet penalty on Fred Warner. On 3rd and 4, Mykel Williams tipped Daniels’ pass to force another punt. However, Malik Mustapha was flagged for illegal contact, giving the Commanders a fresh set of downs. The call went against Mustapha, but the replay showed it was against Renardo Green. Washington converted its first third down of the game in the fourth quarter. A late hit by Odighizuwa tacked on 15 yards. And just like that, it was 1st-and-goal from the nine. Daniels hooked up with Raachad White, who had a step on Deommodore Lenoir, for another touchdown. That made it 23-17. The 49ers got sloppy. After the drive, they committed eight penalties for 63 yards. Daniels was 22-for-27 with a passer rating of 124.8. Their offense was clicking. Could the offense answer back? Purdy couldn’t avoid a free rusher and took a sack on a second-and-long. He sailed a throw on third down. The Niners went three-and-out on back-to-back drives. It’s no coincidence they struggled without Evans. Raheem Morris had enough of Upton Stout. Ashtyn Davis came in at nickel for Stout. Davis gave up a 30-yard completion. Washington scored on the next play, but a penalty negated a 31-yard touchdown run. On 4th-and-8, Washington used a valuable timeout. Romello Height sacked Daniels, but a flag in the secondary once again gifted Washington a fresh set of downs. The flag was on Davis. Height made a great rush. The game would come down to 4th and 3 after a big hit by Mustapha on third down. Mustapha came through again by jarring loose a target at the goal line. The 49ers don’t win this game without his performance. The Commanders had two timeouts. We’ve seen the 49ers be aggressive in these situations, but that was with Evans on the field. On 3rd and 8, the Niners ran the ball and drained the clock. A conservative call that gave Washington the ball back with a minute remaining and a chance to win. It was the offense’s third straight three-and-out. Siran Neal was flagged for kick-catch interference. That put Washington around midfield with 52 seconds remaining. Instead of Stout or Davis, Lenoir moved into the slot with Jack Jones replacing him outside. This follows Davis’s struggles on the previous two drives. Daviels took an intentional grounding penalty after Romello Height got pressure once again. It was costly, as the 10-second run-off left only six seconds remaining. Height and White sacked Daniels on a three-man rush, helping the 49ers escape.

item.title: Baltimore Ravens Sign Record-Setting Kicker to Compete With Tyler Loop
item.description: San Francisco 49ers kicker Jake Moody. Getty The Baltimore Ravens aren’t standing on ceremony at 4-2 and looking up at the Cleveland Browns in the AFC North standings. That includes bringing in competition for starting kicker Tyler Loop. “Sources: The Ravens are signing K Jake Moody to their practice squad, bringing him back as competition,” NFL insider Jordan Schultz wrote on his official X account on Monday. “Moody was with the team earlier this season when Tyler Loop had struggled in camp … (Moody) 26-year-old went 19/23 on FGs last season, including 10/11 in Washington. He also made both of his 50+ yard attempts, with a long of 56 yards.” “The Ravens are once again signing K Jake Moody to their practice squad,” Ravens reporter Kevin Oestricher wrote on his official X account on Monday. “ Moody was with Baltimore briefly during training camp, and will join Tyler Loop in the Ravens’ kicking room again Jesse Minter was frustrated when discussing Loop’s misses on Monday.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Baltimore Ravens Sign Record-Setting Kicker to Compete With Tyler Loop appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Former All-Star Mocks Los Angeles Lakers Title Contending Goals
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 06: Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers watches his team play against the Golden State Warriors from the bench during the first half of their preseason game at Chase Center on October 06, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty The Los Angeles Lakers have a tough season ahead of them with a killer Western Conference slew of playoff teams. At least six teams in the West believe they should contend for an NBA Championship, including the Lakers. However, most pundits rank them significantly behind the top teams of the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs. Former NBA superstar DeMarcus Cousins praised Luka Doncic, but he claimed the Lakers have no chance at all to contend with this roster: “Do I think this is a championship group? No. I think they’re a scary team every single night. I think they can upset some teams this year, but as far as just being that high-level team, contending-type team, I just can’t call it. I don’t see it. I think they got a lot of work to do, but I expect Luka to put up some incredible numbers. It could potentially be an MVP-type season for him, depending on how far he can really carry this group, but I can’t say they’re a better team without (LeBron James).” The big reason cited by Cousins is that the Lakers are just not a better team without James. Taking the chance on Walker Kessler as the third star sees risk involved already, but it gets more concerning when you lose LeBron and a handful of other respected rotation players. Can The Lakers Improve Without LeBron? Criticism towards Lakers General Manager Rob Pelinka started this offseason when fans watched the moves play out in real time. Extending Austin Reaves to a long-term contract and acquiring Kessler from the Utah Jazz were the two biggest moves. Otherwise, the Lakers took some chances by letting players go beyond just LeBron. Role players Rui Hachimura, Marcus Smart , and Luke Kennard all contributed to the Lakers having a strong season last year as a top four seed. New role player additions like Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes are not guaranteed success stories. In fact, many experts think the Lakers have too many players who do the same thing. Most agree with Cousins that this roster will be worse than last season to make contending quite difficult. How The Lakers Can Prove Critics Wrong The biggest thing working in the Lakers’ favor is that Doncic is arguably the best offensive player in the league. Luka is right there with multi-time MVPs Nikola Jokic and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander when it comes to running an effective offense by himself. Teams like the Denver Nuggets , Houston Rockets , and Minnesota Timberwolves are typically also ranked over the Lakers ahead of the upcoming season. Kessler

item.title: Cleveland Guardians 2026 Season Ends After ALCS Game 6 Loss
item.description: The Cleveland Guardians know what it's like to play with their backs against the wall. They did at the end of the regular season just to make the playoffs, and again were in the same position when they fell behind in the ALDS. They were hoping for a little more magic on Monday evening to force a Game 7, but ultimately fell to the Tampa Bay Rays , 7-3, in Game 6, officially ending their playoff run and 2026 season. Cleveland’s biggest need heading into Monday’s elimination game was clear: the Guardians had to get the bats going and somehow find a way to generate more runs than Tampa. Did Cleveland’s lineup struggle that much, or was the Rays’ pitching that good? Either way you look at it, the Guardians just simply didn’t generate enough offense to come out on the team. Peralta wasn’t as dominant as he was in Game 2, and Cleveland certainly had scoring opportunities off the Rays pitcher, but just couldn’t capitalize and get the big hit. He ended up allowing eight baserunners, and Nathaniel Lowe got to him with an RBI single in the top of the sixth inning, which essentially ended his night. Oct 19, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays shortstop Taylor Walls (6) gets the out on Cleveland Guardians shortstop Brayan Rocchio (4) in game six of the ALCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images But when you look at it, Cleveland had chances against Tampa Bay pitching all evening. Unfortunately, just like throughout the series, the Guardians failed to come up with a big hit with runners in scoring position. Even in the top of the eighth inning with the bases loaded, the Guardians needed help from a walk and a hit-by-pitch to score two runs. Brayan Rocchio then struck out on three strikes to end the threat. At the end of the night, both teams tallied seven hits, and the Guardians even ended up with one more base runner than the Rays. However, Cleveland left nine runners on base and were just 1-for-6 with runners in scoring position. Looking at Cleveland’s pitching, there was a lot of discourse about Stephen Vogt’s decision not to start Gavin Williams on short rest in an elimination game. Instead, the Guardians went with a bullpen game. The decision from the Guardians was controversial, but it’s far from what cost them in the end. Through the first six innings of the game, or the same number of innings a starter would have ideally covered, the bullpen only allowed three earned runs. It was the two-run home run from Junior Caminero off Cade Smith and the two-run home run from Yandy Diaz off Hunter Gaddis that ended up being the backbreakers for Cleveland. The Guardians now head into the offseason, reflecting on what went wrong in the last three games and how they can return to this position in 2027.

Count Golden State Warriors star Draymond Green as somebody who is on the fence. Warriors Star Draymond Green Gets Real On 76ers Before Opener vs Knicks Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – JANUARY 02: Draymond Green #23 of the Golden State Warriors matches up against Joel Embiid #21 of the Philadelphia 76ers at Chase Center on January 02, 2025 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) “I think on paper it looks really good. Where I struggle is how does the pieces really fit?” Green said on his podcast this week . “Tyrese Maxey is super fast and gets downhill as good as anyone. How many games does Joel (Embiid) play, because when Joel’s not out there, the paint’s wide open and Tyrese Maxey can get downhill at will. If Joel plays 50 games … How do you ultimately build that chemistry, and no pun intended, that process, to ultimately allow you to reach the pinnacle? Jaylen Brown or Tyrese Maxey? Cause they play two completely different styles of basketball, so when you’re talking about one being the one and flipping back and forth, that’s also going to require other guys to flip their mindset when one is being the one and when the other’s being the one.” Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – JANUARY 02: Draymond Green #23 of the Golden State Warriors boxes out Joel Embiid #21 of the Philadelphia 76ers in the first half at Chase Center on January 02, 2025 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) All valid questions from Green, and those concerns are far from typical. Having multiple players who really only co-starred with one other person, the Sixers have four recent All-Stars trying to share the spotlight. It could end up being a boom-or-bust season for the Sixers. “They could be really good and win it, but I think there is a range,” Green stated. The veteran forward could see the 76ers winning the NBA Championship. But he could also see this new superteam fall victim to the trend and come up flat with a first-round exit. The 76ers will begin their new journey on Tuesday night (October 20) with a matchup against the New York Knicks . Barring any unexpected setbacks, the starting five should be healthy and playing. item.title: ‘Really Happy’ – Johan Ghazali Reflects On Sweet Revenge Against Diego Paez At The Inner Circle 35
item.description: Johan “Jojo” Ghazali came to Bangkok with serious unfinished business against Diego Paez , and he left with the exact result he needed. The 19-year-old Malaysian-American sensation defeated the Colombian-American star via unanimous decision after a grueling three-round flyweight Muay Thai firefight in the co-main event of The Inner Circle 35 this past Friday, October 16, streaming live from historic Lumpinee Stadium via live.onefc.com . View this post on Instagram The definitive result ends a two-fight losing streak for Ghazali and settles a bitter score that had been sitting unresolved since last year, when Paez claimed a narrow split decision in their first meeting. The rematch went the other way entirely. With nine victories in ONE Championship now on his record and a 28-11 professional mark, the teenager from Rentap Muaythai Gym and Superbon Training Camp answered the most pressing questions facing him with a clear, three-round statement. The gap between their first encounter and this rematch was visible across all three rounds. Ghazali looked noticeably more composed, more precise, and far more willing to engage strictly on his terms rather than merely reacting to the chaos Paez creates. He told onefc.com: “How do I feel? Yeah, I’m really happy! Really, really happy. I feel like I’ve improved — improved a lot. Well, I’m not perfect yet, not at my absolute best, but definitely better. I’m improved but not entirely satisfied yet.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Ghazali carried genuine respect for Paez into this high-stakes rematch. The Colombian-American is a physically imposing, high-output opponent who brings the exact same relentless energy and power from the opening bell to the final seconds of round three — a durable quality that makes him a legitimate problem for anyone in the flyweight division. But “Jojo” had already identified the root cause of his previous loss, and the ultimate difference on Friday night was not about the opponent across the ring. item.content:encoded: Johan “Jojo” Ghazali came to Bangkok with serious unfinished business against Diego Paez , and he left with the exact result he needed. The 19-year-old Malaysian-American sensation defeated the Colombian-American star via unanimous decision after a grueling three-round flyweight Muay Thai firefight in the co-main event of The Inner Circle 35 this past Friday, October 16, streaming live from historic Lumpinee Stadium via live.onefc.com . View this post on Instagram The definitive result ends a two-fight losing streak for Ghazali and settles a bitter score that had been sitting unresolved since last year, when Paez claimed a narrow split decision in their first meeting. The rematch went the other way entirely. With nine victories in ONE Championship now on his record and a 28-11 professional mark, the teenager from Rentap Muaythai Gym and Superbon Training Camp answered the most pressing questions facing him with a clear, three-round statement. The gap between their first encounter and this rematch was visible across all three rounds. Ghazali looked noticeably more composed, more precise, and far more willing to engage strictly on his terms rather than merely reacting to the chaos Paez creates. He told onefc.com: “How do I feel? Yeah, I’m really happy! Really, really happy. I feel like I’ve improved — improved a lot. Well, I’m not perfect yet, not at my absolute best, but definitely better. I’m improved but not entirely satisfied yet.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Ghazali carried genuine respect for Paez into this high-stakes rematch. The Colombian-American is a physically imposing, high-output opponent who brings the exact same relentless energy and power from the opening bell to the final seconds of round three — a durable quality that makes him a legitimate problem for anyone in the flyweight division. But “Jojo” had already identified the root cause of his previous loss, and the ultimate difference on Friday night was not about the opponent across the ring. It was about his own internal adjustments. Ghazali explained: “Diego is good. He’s got weapons, he hits hard, and he maintains his energy and heavy strikes from round one through three. Diego is solid, but honestly, in my last fight against him, my game plan wasn’t good. I was nervous and rushing too much. Yeah, so this fight was definitely an improvement.” View this post on Instagram The vital corner advice Ghazali received between rounds from reigning ONE Featherweight Kickboxing World Champion Superbon directly addressed the specific mental block that caused problems in their first meeting and threatened to resurface in the opening exchanges of the rematch. Getting comfortable with that aggressive shift mid-contest required exactly the kind of deep trust in his mentor — and himself — that separates elite fighters who actively grow from those who simply repeat the same mistakes. He said: “In the first round, Superbon told me, ‘Stay calm. Don’t rush, don’t jump around too much, and don’t back up too much either.’ He also said, ‘Don’t be afraid of getting [hit with] punches. If you get hit, it’s fine. As a fighter, you can’t be scared of punches.’ If you watched my last fight, I blocked and guarded really well, but if you just block well without throwing any strikes, it doesn’t work. “Superbon told me, ‘Don’t be overly cautious. If you get hit or even knocked out, don’t overthink it — fighters can’t fear getting hit.’ So I was like… well, it’s not that I wasn’t afraid at all, but I guarded less and threw more strikes instead.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Ghazali Targets Ramadan Rematch, Offers Shimon Some Ringside Advice With the Diego Paez rematch officially settled, Johan Ghazali’s attention turned immediately to what he wants next, and the name at the very top of his list was not a surprise to anyone following the 19-year-old’s ONE career closely. His controversial bout with Ramadan “The Scorpion” Ondash in July left a bitter feeling that has not gone away. Ghazali remains unhappy with the result and firmly believes the fans share his deep desire to see the two violently meet again. A rematch is the specific fight he wants most, and he makes absolutely no effort to disguise it. Before getting to that, though, he had a piece of unsolicited advice for Shimon Yoshinari , who is set to face Ondash in the 2026-2027 ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix quarterfinals in November at The Inner Circle 38 . Ghazali’s advice drew directly from his own frustrating experience in July, when Ondash’s mouthpiece repeatedly fell out during their intense contest. The Rentap Muaythai Gym product said: “I’m a fighter, I can fight anyone. If I had to fight Ramadan… actually, no. But if I were Shimon, I’d check his mouthpiece first! I’d check it beforehand. “If I were Shimon, during the walkout, after applying Vaseline, I’d check the mouthpiece first — put it in, slap him on the face first, and see: does it fall out? Does it come loose? If it falls out, no fight. If it stays in, we fight! Yeah, but honestly, I can fight anyone. Whether Ramadan wants it or Shimon wants it, anyone — I’m not scared of anybody.” View this post on Instagram Ghazali made it crystal clear that a rematch with Ramadan is the bout he wants above all else. He wasn’t satisfied with how their July encounter played out, and he knows the global fanbase wants to see them run it back. The unfinished business with Ondash is very real, the desire to settle it is entirely genuine, and the teenager left Lumpinee Stadium on Friday night with a crucial victory that keeps him firmly entrenched in the conversation for the biggest flyweight matchups the division has to offer. He concluded: “One name? I really want to face Ramadan. I wasn’t happy — I was really unsatisfied with our last fight. I felt like I won that fight, but it just wasn’t right. I think the fans want to see it too. So if I get to fight Ramadan next, that’d be great. But if not, anyone is fine.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Source

item.title: UEFA Champions League Matchday 3 Predictions Including Barcelona vs PSG
item.description: IMAGO / PsnewZ FOOTBALL : Paris Saint Germain Vs Arsenal - Ligue des Champions - 07/05/2025 Joie Paris Saint Germain - Desire Doue PSG - Luis Enrique PSG ParisFrance PUBLICATIONxNOTxINxFRAxBEL Copyright: xMichtofx | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Alex Richards, LWOF Editor Matchday 3 of the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League has arrived. We have two of the brightest stars in Europe, Barcelona vs PSG facing off, Atletico Madrid, Manchester City and Liverpool are not to be forgotten either. Here is your preview and predictions for all nine matches on Tuesday. UEFA Champions League Tuesday Predictions Slavia Prague at Fenerbahce Fenerbahce have been flying in Turkiye but looked terrible at Villa Park last week, conceding six to Aston Villa. Slavia Prague will be an easier opponent, and they are at home against the Czech leaders. Igoh Ogbu is out for Slavia, Marco Asensio misses for Fenerbahce. Fenerbahce should manage to settle themselves and score again. Prediction: Fenerbahce 2-0 Borussia Dortmund at Sabah Sabah at home, the toast of Azerbaijan, can they pull off a massive upset against a struggling Dortmund side? Dortmund will be without Konstantinos Karetsas and are scoreless in their last two games. Sabah has talent and should make this difficult for at least an hour. Prediction: Dortmund 1-0 Villarreal at Liverpool Villarreal got a result against Napoli last week, but a trip to Anfield isn’t easy. Liverpool know how to score, but defensively there’s trouble. Jeremie Frimpong, Conor Bradley and Dominik Szoboszlai will miss. Alexander Isak can be the difference maker for Liverpool though, and they can outscore a lot of teams. Prediction: Liverpool 4-2 Liverpool FC v Atletico de Madrid – UEFA Champions League 2026 27 League Phase MD1 Jeremy Jacquet of Liverpool running during the UEFA Champions League 2026 27 League Phase MD1 match between Liverpool FC and Atletico de Madrid at Anfield on September 9, 2026 in Liverpool, England. Liverpool Anfield England United Kingdom Copyright: xAllstarxPicturexLibraryxLtdx AEK Athens at Manchester City if Erling Haaland can play, it’s even more of an advantage to Manchester City , if he’s still unfit, they are likely still better than AEK, a side unbeaten in Greece and fresh. Antoine Semenyo will miss two months for Manchester City but they have enough depth to sort things out. Prediction: Manchester City 3-1 Barcelona at PSG The two best teams in continental Europe, Barcelona move through the gears and dominate the opposition through the varied talents of Lamine Yamal, Raphinha, who will return to the starting lineup, and more. Barca will be without Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde, there’s trouble in the back. PSG at their best are still Champions of Europe and at home, Nuno Mendes is out though, a defence also looking vulnerable, against the best attack in the world. Barcelona may not win it all this season, but doing the double, beating PSG on Tuesday, and Real Madrid on Sunday actually feels plausible right now. P

Liverpool Anfield England United Kingdom Copyright: xAllstarxPicturexLibraryxLtdx AEK Athens at Manchester City if Erling Haaland can play, it’s even more of an advantage to Manchester City , if he’s still unfit, they are likely still better than AEK, a side unbeaten in Greece and fresh. Antoine Semenyo will miss two months for Manchester City but they have enough depth to sort things out. Barcelona may not win it all this season, but doing the double, beating PSG on Tuesday, and Real Madrid on Sunday actually feels plausible right now. Prediction: Barcelona 3-2 Bodo/Glimt at Napoli Napoli have struggled in Europe and domestically, Massimiliano Allegri could lose his job, and there’s no David Neres and other first choice players. Bodo/Glimt at home pulled it off against Dortmund and have real momentum. They should be able to grind out a point away. Prediction: 1-1 Draw Atletico Madrid at Stuttgart The depth and quality of La Liga will be tested here. Atletico Madrid have been good in Spain, and competitive in Europe through two games, Stuttgart are in bad shape in the Bundesliga, but strong in Europe to start. Stuttgart’s backline without Ameen Al-Dakhil and Dan-Axel Zagadou will invite Atletico to attack and they can come away with a point. Prediction: 2-2 Draw PSV at FC Porto A fun matchup that tests the quality of the top of the Portuguese and Dutch leagues this season. Porto are hosts, and perfect domestically. PSV are missing Ricardo Pepi, Alassane Plea and Sam Lammers. Jan Bednarek returns to Porto’s backline and makes it even harder for PSV to score. Porto should shine in this one. Prediction: FC Porto 2-1 Slovan Bratislava at Roma Roma’s defensive disaster, a set piece letdown leading to defeat against Real Madrid. That was painful medicine to swallow, though they are favored at home against Slovan Bratislava. AS Roma have a long injury list, including Paulo Dybala, Slovan look outmatched against quality European sides, it’s still Roma as favorites, but you can’t fully trust them. item.title: NBA Predictions 2026-27: Who will be champs? Our experts make their picks
item.description: With the 2026-27 NBA season here, it's time to make our championship predictions. Who will win it all? Our writers make their picks. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Who will win the East? Kelly Iko: New York Knicks. I have a gut feeling that some of New York's very public, very unfortunate and very off-court stuff could be a distraction, but this team hasn't changed too much and still has the wherewithal to go the distance. The other challengers — Raptors, Pacers, 76ers, Celtics, Pistons, Cavs — have too many questions in one department or the other. There's not a true hole on this Knicks roster or coaching staff, which is always the key. Dan Devine: New York Knicks. I can't believe we've arrived at a place where I trust the Knicks more than any other team in the field, but we have. Yes, they've logged a ton of miles over the past two seasons, and yes, we're in an era where conference champions don't tend to repeat. But while I'm only guessing at the ceilings of the other Eastern contending hopefuls, I know how high a level the Knicks can hit. For now, that's enough. (Ethan Palowitz/Yahoo Sports Illustration) Tom Haberstroh: Philadelphia 76ers. You can probably talk me into something like six different teams here. The East is absolutely loaded. So far, LeBron James and Joel Embiid are healthy. Until I hear otherwise on that health front, I'll go with the team with four All-NBA guys, a championship-winning head coach and sneaky depth. Steve Jones: New York Knicks. The East will finally get respect this season. The competition will be stacked: The Knicks, Cavs and Pistons have continuity, the Sixers, Heat and Raptors made moves, the Celtics never leave, and Tyrese Haliburton is back! I believe the Sixers are absolutely built for the playoffs and am curious where their regular season adventure lands them, but I had the Knicks last year, changed the pick at the last minute to Cleveland (that got funny), and will not be doing that this year. Give me the Knicks building on their championship formula. Nekias Duncan: Boston Celtics. There are plenty of great options to choose from, highlighted by the defending champs who lost [checks notes] one (1) player from their top-10 playoff rotation. I'm just a huge believer in what Boston has built structurally, headlined by an MVP-caliber talent in Jayson Tatum, who I think is primed for a huge year. They shoot, they rebound, they defend, they don't turn the ball over … they have my eye right now. NBA Predictions 2026-27: MVP, Rookie of the Year and more awards Who will win the West? item.content:encoded: With the 2026-27 NBA season here, it's time to make our championship predictions. Who will win it all? Our writers make their picks. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Who will win the East? Kelly Iko: New York Knicks. I have a gut feeling that some of New York's very public, very unfortunate and very off-court stuff could be a distraction, but this team hasn't changed too much and still has the wherewithal to go the distance. The other challengers — Raptors, Pacers, 76ers, Celtics, Pistons, Cavs — have too many questions in one department or the other. There's not a true hole on this Knicks roster or coaching staff, which is always the key. Dan Devine: New York Knicks. I can't believe we've arrived at a place where I trust the Knicks more than any other team in the field, but we have. Yes, they've logged a ton of miles over the past two seasons, and yes, we're in an era where conference champions don't tend to repeat. But while I'm only guessing at the ceilings of the other Eastern contending hopefuls, I know how high a level the Knicks can hit. For now, that's enough. (Ethan Palowitz/Yahoo Sports Illustration) Tom Haberstroh: Philadelphia 76ers. You can probably talk me into something like six different teams here. The East is absolutely loaded. So far, LeBron James and Joel Embiid are healthy. Until I hear otherwise on that health front, I'll go with the team with four All-NBA guys, a championship-winning head coach and sneaky depth. Steve Jones: New York Knicks. The East will finally get respect this season. The competition will be stacked: The Knicks, Cavs and Pistons have continuity, the Sixers, Heat and Raptors made moves, the Celtics never leave, and Tyrese Haliburton is back! I believe the Sixers are absolutely built for the playoffs and am curious where their regular season adventure lands them, but I had the Knicks last year, changed the pick at the last minute to Cleveland (that got funny), and will not be doing that this year. Give me the Knicks building on their championship formula. Nekias Duncan: Boston Celtics. There are plenty of great options to choose from, highlighted by the defending champs who lost [checks notes] one (1) player from their top-10 playoff rotation. I'm just a huge believer in what Boston has built structurally, headlined by an MVP-caliber talent in Jayson Tatum, who I think is primed for a huge year. They shoot, they rebound, they defend, they don't turn the ball over … they have my eye right now. NBA Predictions 2026-27: MVP, Rookie of the Year and more awards Who will win the West? Duncan: Oklahoma City Thunder. That the Thunder dealt with as many injuries as they did and still managed to flirt with 70 wins and go seven in the Western Conference finals against an alien — while having a fourth-quarter lead! — is a testament to how great this team is. There's top-end talent to be excited about, internal development to bank on, elite coaching on the sidelines, and they should have a chip on their shoulder after how last season ended. Haberstroh: San Antonio Spurs. A healthy Jalen Williams may have tilted the scales in OKC's favor last May, but I just can't shake how inconsequential Chet Holmgren looked against Wemby. I'm going with the still-rising Spurs. Jones: San Antonio Spurs. The Spurs are going to have to deal with a different level of attention after surprising the league last year. But I feel like that, combined with an endless desire for revenge, ends up helping them out more than anything. They make it back to the Finals. Devine: Oklahoma City Thunder. I'll take the Thunder, getting their lick back in a Western Conference finals rematch with the Spurs. Iko: San Antonio Spurs. San Antonio has identified its mortal enemy, and nothing will take the Spurs off the collision course for a rematch. Who will be the NBA champs? Devine: Thunder over Knicks. New York takes the title defense as far as it can go before running out of gas, but Oklahoma City stakes its claim as the league's premier team, and SGA becomes one of just seven players ever with multiple regular-season and Finals MVPs, joining Michael Jordan, LeBron James, Tim Duncan, Magic Johnson, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Larry Bird. Pretty decent company. Duncan: Thunder over Celtics. The star power of SGA and Tatum. The coaching battle of Mark Daigneault and Joe Mazzulla. The pageantry of a Paul George "revenge" series, and the bounceback campaign of Jalen Williams. Derrick White and Cason Wallace flying around. Alex Caruso and Hugo González also flying around. A fun, stylistic clash of the frontcourts — and plenty of screening goodness for nerds like me. I'd love every second of this. Ultimately, I think the Thunder are the best team in the league, and should be favored to add another title to the chamber. Iko: Spurs over Knicks. We were treated to an absolute feast of a Finals a few months ago. Brilliant coaching, subtle in-game tweaks, star moments, press conference soundbites and more. Let's do this again, shall we? The only difference is I think San Antonio, now with Tobias Harris in tow and a new lineup look, has the tools to withstand the brilliance of Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, and OG Anunoby. (Sleeper prediction: A key member of this Knicks team gets traded by February.) Jones: Spurs over Knicks. Who doesn't love a good rematch: The Knicks and their ability to poke at the Spurs' defensive rotations (and moving Wembanyama around the board), and the Spurs working to showcase an improved offensive attack and erase the memory of last year. It would be a blast, and I think the Spurs take it. Haberstroh: Spurs over Sixers. Big Vic finally gets crowned as the champ. Rookie of the Year. All-Star in Year 2. Top 3 in MVP in Year 3. Champ in Year 4. Seems like a natural order of things. Only two other players in NBA history can claim that exact progression. Bob Pettit and Dave Cowens. It hasn't happened in over 50 years. Wemby is that dude.

item.title: Ryan Reaves Pulls Curtain Back On Time With Maple Leafs
item.description: Photo by Claus Andersen/Getty Images Getty TORONTO, CANADA - MARCH 02: Ryan Reaves #75 of the Toronto Maple Leafs and Matt Rempe #73 of the New York Rangers square off at centre ice for a fightduring the third period at Scotiabank Arena on March 02, 2024 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Chris Tanouye/Getty Images) Former Toronto Maple Leafs enforcer Ryan Reaves announced his retirement from the NHL last month, ending his career that spanned 16 total season and multiple clubs, including a stop with the Maple Leafs. Reaves, who accumulated over 1,000 penalty minutes during his career, is now pulling the curtain back on his time while with the Maple Leafs. Former Toronto Maple Leafs Forward Ryan Reaves Breaks Silence Of His Time With The Team TORONTO, CANADA – MARCH 02: Ryan Reaves #75 of the Toronto Maple Leafs and Matt Rempe #73 of the New York Rangers square off at centre ice for a fightduring the third period at Scotiabank Arena on March 02, 2024 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Chris Tanouye/Getty Images) Reaves, who did see time with another Original 6 club during his time in the NHL when he played for the New York Rangers, said that it was a great experience for him to play for a historic club like the Maple Leafs, and that he was treated well during his time with the team. “I enjoyed my time in Toronto,” Reaves said while making a guest appearance on the JD Bunkis podcast . “I didn’t have my best part of my career there, for sure. There was a lot of ups and downs for me, but I think it was everything I expected. “The team treated you better than any other team in the league,” he continued. “There’s a reason why wearing that jersey is so special, because how they treat you. You have to earn the right to play there, but it was cool. Throwing on the Original Six jersey and playing in front of those fans, it was fun.” Ryan Reaves Announced His Retirement On Instagram With a special post on Instagram last month, Reaves announced that he was retiring from the NHL. His message began: “Dear Hockey, It’s hard to put into words what you meant to me. What you mean to me. I had dreams of being an athlete. Football, hockey—it didn’t matter. I learned at a young age that I just wanted to lay people out. The physical part of sports was what I was always drawn to. I knew that’s what I wanted, but tell 10-year-old Reavo he was going to play in the NHL for 16 seasons? I don’t think he’d believe you.” He concluded by announcing that he was stepping away from the game, while joking that “the corners are a little safer today”. “Today, I retire from the sport I’ve loved since I was 5 years old. It was a hell of a ride. Thank you to everyone who supported me throughout this journey. There are too many to single out, so you’ll hear from me at some point. I may not be on the ice anymore, but I know I will always be close to hockey in one way or another. You can rest easy knowing the corners are a little safer today. Mic drop, gloves drop. Reavo out.” Dur
item.content:encoded: Photo by Claus Andersen/Getty Images Getty TORONTO, CANADA - MARCH 02: Ryan Reaves #75 of the Toronto Maple Leafs and Matt Rempe #73 of the New York Rangers square off at centre ice for a fightduring the third period at Scotiabank Arena on March 02, 2024 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Chris Tanouye/Getty Images) Former Toronto Maple Leafs enforcer Ryan Reaves announced his retirement from the NHL last month, ending his career that spanned 16 total season and multiple clubs, including a stop with the Maple Leafs. Reaves, who accumulated over 1,000 penalty minutes during his career, is now pulling the curtain back on his time while with the Maple Leafs. Former Toronto Maple Leafs Forward Ryan Reaves Breaks Silence Of His Time With The Team TORONTO, CANADA – MARCH 02: Ryan Reaves #75 of the Toronto Maple Leafs and Matt Rempe #73 of the New York Rangers square off at centre ice for a fightduring the third period at Scotiabank Arena on March 02, 2024 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Chris Tanouye/Getty Images) Reaves, who did see time with another Original 6 club during his time in the NHL when he played for the New York Rangers, said that it was a great experience for him to play for a historic club like the Maple Leafs, and that he was treated well during his time with the team. “I enjoyed my time in Toronto,” Reaves said while making a guest appearance on the JD Bunkis podcast . “I didn’t have my best part of my career there, for sure. There was a lot of ups and downs for me, but I think it was everything I expected. “The team treated you better than any other team in the league,” he continued. “There’s a reason why wearing that jersey is so special, because how they treat you. You have to earn the right to play there, but it was cool. Throwing on the Original Six jersey and playing in front of those fans, it was fun.” Ryan Reaves Announced His Retirement On Instagram With a special post on Instagram last month, Reaves announced that he was retiring from the NHL. His message began: “Dear Hockey, It’s hard to put into words what you meant to me. What you mean to me. I had dreams of being an athlete. Football, hockey—it didn’t matter. I learned at a young age that I just wanted to lay people out. The physical part of sports was what I was always drawn to. I knew that’s what I wanted, but tell 10-year-old Reavo he was going to play in the NHL for 16 seasons? I don’t think he’d believe you.” He concluded by announcing that he was stepping away from the game, while joking that “the corners are a little safer today”. “Today, I retire from the sport I’ve loved since I was 5 years old. It was a hell of a ride. Thank you to everyone who supported me throughout this journey. There are too many to single out, so you’ll hear from me at some point. I may not be on the ice anymore, but I know I will always be close to hockey in one way or another. You can rest easy knowing the corners are a little safer today. Mic drop, gloves drop. Reavo out.” During his career, Reaves played in 962 regular season games, scoring 66 goals with 74 assists, while racking up 1,137 penalty minutes. He also had three goals, six assists, and 116 penalty minutes in 113 Stanley Cup Playoff games. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Ryan Reaves Pulls Curtain Back On Time With Maple Leafs appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: ‘If I Were a Betting Man’ — Media Analyst Predicts 3-Time Pro Bowler Will Replace Troy Aikman in ESPN’s MNF Booth Alongside Joe Buck
item.description: Nov 3, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; Television commentator Troy Aikman speaks before the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. © Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Troy Aikman and Joe Buck have spent 25 straight NFL seasons together in the booth, talking football week after week. However, that could soon come to an end, as there’s been a lot of talk about the iconic duo going their separate ways. Buck recently agreed to a six-year contract extension that will keep him at ESPN through 2032. Aikman’s contract, meanwhile, is set to expire after the 2026 season, following Super Bowl LXI in February 2027. He recently confirmed that he will become a broadcasting free agent after the current NFL season. So, who could replace Aikman as Buck’s broadcast partner? Speculation is already building, and one media analyst has made a strong case for a potential replacement. Jimmy Traina Predicts Greg Olsen Could Replace Troy Aikman at ESPN Speaking on “The Traina Thoughts Podcast,” prominent sports journalist and media analyst Jimmy Traina suggested that Olsen is the one he’d bet on to replace Aikman at ESPN next year. “It’s going to be Greg Olsen,” Traina said confidently . “If I were a betting man, it’s going to be Joe Buck and Greg Olsen. Now, can things change where ESPN reaches out to Troy and says, ‘Let’s get this deal done’? Yes.” Traina noted that there’s always a chance for a last-ditch effort. Maybe Aikman is playing a bit of hardball, knowing ESPN likely wants to keep its star duo together. However, Aikman told Traina that ESPN hasn’t made any attempt to negotiate a new deal with him. “Why would there be no negotiations and no talks with the No. 1 analyst in the game, the best analyst in the game, in your Super Bowl year, after you had year after year after year a subpar Monday night booth, now you have the best booth in the game,” Traina added. “Just that fact alone that there have been no negotiations tells you everything you need to know.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor While the lack of negotiations may be telling, as Traina hinted, there’s always a chance ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro makes a concerted effort to retain Aikman before any changes are made. But for now, Traina believes the job is Olsen’s… if he wants it. “Jimmy Pitaro, the president of ESPN, could call up Troy’s agent and say, ‘Let’s get a deal done,’ and something can change,” Traina speculated. “I don’t know what the chances are of that happening. I would put them low because you would think it would already have been done by now.” Many NFL fans would welcome Olsen, a three-time Pro Bowl tight end, getting a chance to call primetime games, even if it means saying goodbye to Aikman in the broadcast booth. item.title: Vote. The Republic's High School Athletes of the Week, Oct. 12-17
item.description: Here are this week's nominees for The Arizona Republic's boys and girls athletes of the week, sponsored by Diamond Kitchen & Bath. Nominees are based on performances in Arizona Interscholastic Association-sanctioned sports the previous week. Vote for the top selection in each of our polls below. Voting will close at 6 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 23, and winners will be announced the next day on azcentral.com and in The Arizona Republic on Sunday, Oct. 25. Submit a weekly nominee at static.azcentral.com/sports/high-schools/nominations/ ). Here are this week's nominees, followed by poll (scroll down on poll to vote): Girls Kallie James, Avondale St. John Paul Catholic II, flag football, Fr.: She had four receptions for 130 yards and one touchdown on offense and recorded one interception on defense in a 28-6 win over Kingman on Oct. 13. Delaney Barbee, Anthem Boulder Creek, swimming, Sr.: She won the 50 free (23.05 seconds), 100 free (51.05) and 200 free (1:52.41) at the Forktoberfest on Oct. 17, setting the state-leading time in all three events. Ashlyn Quiri, Oro Valley Ironwood Ridge, volleyball, Sr.: She set the Southern Arizona career kills record during a 3-0 win over Douglas on Oct. 15, hitting 1,523 career kills during the match. Boys Micah Newcombe, Mesa Dobson, football, Sr.: He ran the ball 39 times for 500 yards and seven touchdowns in a 62-35 win over Paradise Valley on Oct. 16. He also had 38 receiving yards and a touchdown. Yonah Beatty, Whiteriver Alchesay, cross-country, Sr.: He won the Combs Invite on Oct. 14, running the 5,000-meter course in 15:30.5 to move up to No. 8 in the state for the distance. Nolan Guidry, Phoenix Brophy Prep, swimming, So.: He won the 50 free (20.92) at the Forktoberfest on Oct. 17, moving up to No. 2 in the state for the event, and was on the winning 200 free relay team (1:27.14). He also finished second in the 100 free (45.85), moving up to No. 2 in the state for that event. Support local journalism: Subscribe to azcentral.com toda y. This article originally appeared on Arizona Republic: Vote. The Republic's High School Athletes of the Week, Oct. 12-17
